subject: Blended uptime & latency safeguard — SLA negotiation
messages:
From: Priyanka Singh <priyanka.s@edgewave.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Susan Lee <susan.lee@cornell-law.com>, contracts@edgewave.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:18:00 -0800
Subject: SLA — uptime floor & monthly credit ask

Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to get the SLA back to them with a few specific asks so legal can move toward signature:

- Lower the standard uptime floor to 99.90% for the first 3 months post-go-live (we expect ramp).
- Provide a monthly credit schedule tied to calendar month uptime, and ensure credits are capped at 60% of the monthly bill.
- Include a headline p95 latency commitment for inference requests routed to hosted endpoints (we're seeing p95 sensitivity in our production workload).

I've attached our internal SLA request template (Edgewave_SLA_Request_v2.pdf). Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept these terms or propose alternatives?

We'd like to finalize by mid-December to hit our Jan 1 deployment.

Thanks,
Priyanka Singh
Head of Procurement, Edgewave Inc.
pri yanka.s@edgewave.com

Attachment: Edgewave_SLA_Request_v2.pdf (pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Priyanka Singh <priyanka.s@edgewave.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLA — uptime floor & monthly credit ask

Priyanka —

Appreciate the clarity and the template. Quick read-through and here's what we can do and where we'd ask for a middle ground: 

Proposed approach (short):
- Baseline uptime: Redwood proposes 99.95% standard uptime (measured monthly), with a 3-month phased grace where credit triggers are delayed by one month to allow for traffic shaping and cache warm-up.
- Blended safeguard: rather than reducing the floor, we propose keeping 99.95% but adding a latency-based safeguard: if p95 latency for inference goes above the agreed threshold (see below), an elevated remedy ladder kicks in.
- Latency commitment: p95 inference latency (API egress to client-observed) of 300ms for primary region (US). We can provide regional adjustments for EU/APAC.
- Monthly credits: remedy tiers tied to calendar-month uptime bands; cap at 50% of the monthly invoice (we can move to 55% in the first quarter only if Edgewave takes Dedicated capacity).

Why this structure? It protects your production experience (latency matters) while avoiding a lower availability floor that significantly increases operational exposure and ripple-credit risk for both parties. 

Next steps:
- I'll attach a redline with the blended safeguard language for legal to review.
- Ben will follow up on measurement windows and instrumentation (how p95 is measured).
- If acceptable, we'll prepare the final PDF for signature and share a DocuSign link.

Can you confirm whether the cap at 50% would be acceptable as a starting point?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0147

Attachment: SLA_redline_v1.pdf (pdf)

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Priyanka Singh <priyanka.s@edgewave.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:06:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLA — uptime floor & monthly credit ask

Quick technical note — Priyanka / Edgewave team:

A couple items our SRE/legal teams will insist on clarifying in the redline so there are no surprises in measurement: 
- Measurement window: uptime calculated on a calendar-month basis using Redwood's monitoring with a 5m sampling cadence; we'll include examples for pro-rata partial-month calculation.
- Latency measurement: p95 computed from request timing at Redwood's egress; we can optionally include customer-observed p95 if Edgewave runs the SDK telemetry and shares a signed sampling feed.
- Incident classification: planned maintenance windows (we propose two 2-hour monthly windows) are carve-outs; emergency maintenance will have accelerated notifications.

If that sounds reasonable I can include sample calculation rows in the final doc.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com

From: Priyanka Singh <priyanka.s@edgewave.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Susan Lee <susan.lee@cornell-law.com>, contracts@edgewave.com
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 11:24:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLA — uptime floor & monthly credit ask

Marissa/Ben —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the proposed alternative. A couple points from our side: 
- The procurement team is uncomfortable with 99.95% as the baseline for a public hosted product; the business case we ran assumes 99.90% for the ramp period.
- We like the blended approach (availability + latency), but want the p95 to be customer-observed where possible. If Redwood can commit to an instrumentation/telemetry exchange (signed feed) for the first 2 months, we can accept your higher uptime floor provided the credit cap is increased during our ramp.
- Regarding monthly cap: procurement will agree to 50% only if the latency safeguard is customer-observed and we get a one-time credit buffer for month one to address cutover risk.

We are prepared to execute the MSA (DocuSign) once SLA wording and credit caps are finalized — legal is standing by.

Link to our procurement portal purchase order: https://procurement.edgewave.com/purchase/orders/78912

Best,
Priyanka

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Susan Lee <susan.lee@cornell-law.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 09:42:00 -0800
Subject: Final proposed SLA language & next steps (signature-ready)

Priyanka / Susan —

Thanks for the call yesterday. Per our discussion, attached is a signature-ready PDF (Final_SLA_for_signature.pdf) that implements the blended uptime/latency safeguard and the phased exceptions we discussed. Key points below (TL;DR):

- Standard uptime: 99.95% measured monthly (Redwood monitoring) with an operationally defined 3-month ramp carve-out: during months 1–3 the remedy ladder will not be enforced until the second month of the ramp (this provides a one-month buffer for cutover issues).
- Latency safeguard: p95 inference latency threshold = 300ms (primary US region). For the first 60 days, Redwood will provide a signed telemetry feed so Edgewave can validate customer-observed p95. If customer-observed p95 breaches the threshold and Redwood's telemetry confirms the issue, the elevated remedy ladder applies.
- Monthly credits: tiered bands (example in doc) with pro-rata calculation and a cap at 50% of the monthly invoice. One-time first-month buffer: an additional discretionary credit equal to 10% of month-one charges if cutover-related systemic errors occur (details in section 4.2).
- Maintenance carve-outs: two scheduled 2-hour maintenance windows per month per region; emergency maintenance with 1-hour notice when possible.

Action items:
1) Priyanka/legal: confirm the telemetry exchange approach and whether the 50% cap + 10% buffer meets procurement approval.
2) Redwood/legal (Laura): will take any final redlines from Susan and return within 48 hours.
3) Marissa: If approved, I'll circulate the DocuSign link and target signature the same week.

Note: attachments include examples of pro-rata calculations and a sample credit schedule.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0147
